leadText:
A Maid (Japanese: メイド Maid) is a type of Pokémon Trainer that debuted in . They are depicted as young women in typical maid servant clothing.

They appear in in Mr. Backlot's when the player decides to take the 5-Maid Knockout Exact-Turn Attack Challenge. Its objective is to beat all five maids in a certain amount of turns. The prize for winning the challenge is a battle with Celeste or Liam. Each of them has a different lucky color and they specialize in training .

In , they use Pokémon from the . In the Battle Subway, they specialize in the final Evolutions of first partner Pokémon. In , they appear in the Battle Chateau although they appear as a , , , or . They also appear in the Battle Maison going by their original name. They gain a male counterpart in s.

It should be noted that at the time the episode aired, the Maid Trainer class did not exist yet, and Monica was merely based on the overworld sprites of the maids in .

===Pokémon Adventures===
==== ====
One of Mr. Backlot's Maids appeared in Suffering Psyduck. She informed Mr. Backlot of the arrival of his guest, and also gave a Soothe Bell as thanks for visiting the .

==== ====
A Maid appeared in Dream a Little Dream as one of the 32 participants of the tournament, going through . She was eventually defeated off-panel, eliminating her from the tournament.

==== ====
A Maid appeared with a in Dancing Vivillon, thanking Cassius for fixing the Battle Chateau's PC Box.
 

====Pokémon====
 

==Trivia==
When defeated, the Maids in the 5-Maid Knockout Exact-Turn Attack Challenge all say the same—"You're so strong!"—adding only an additional exclamation mark for each maid defeated.
One of those Maids is Elena (Japanese: ヘレン Helen), who reappears in Kalos hotels in , offering to trade the player an for any Pokémon. The names are the same in Japanese, English, and Korean, but different in French, German, Italian, and Spanish.
When a Maid is battled at the , she will be shown as a in , as the Maid class did not exist in those versions.
Maids appeared in the Battle Pike in Pokémon Emerald, although they cannot be battled.
In the Battle Chateau, Maid Julia is shown to be a robot, making her the first robotic Trainer in the core series games.
